content:
Whenever possible push the center pin from the inside. But don't push out the collet. Then you can pull out the pin until you feel a indent. Do it for all rivets on the panel, and then you can push out the panel. 
Now you have all rivets stored in place where they should be, and it makes it a lot easier to put them in again.

OK, in this case on the top panel, it doesn't matter since it won't be reused. But it's good for all the other panels.
no real need to have rivets in the top panel at all really it just sits there
a plastic razor blade works great, and most people already have those for getting prints off the sheet

You can carefully remove the rivets using a small side-cutting plier. The snap rivet remover and others wear out so quickly that they stop working properly after just a few rivets. This method also works much better than using the needle-nose pliers shown in the picture.

replies.content: Thank you for your comment. We had to mention the needle-nose pliers because that is a tool you received with the printer. Removing the rivets with side cutters and other methods are possible. Feel free to remove the rivets in a way that suits you best and that will not damage the printer.
